campbell.title: Campbell City Council — August 18, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered several administrative items, including naming voting delegates for the 2026 League of California Cities annual conference and amending an agreement for city clerk services. The Council also considered accepting a grant on behalf of the police department, presented by the police captain, and reviewed a governance update on the BART Silicon Valley project.
keyTopics: Designation of voting delegates for the 2026 League of California Cities annual conference
Resolution amending the first amended agreement for city clerk services
Grant acceptance on behalf of the police department, presented by the police captain
Governance update on the BART Silicon Valley project

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — August 19, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered a routine mix of contracts and administrative items, including janitorial services, irrigation maintenance, a GIS consultant contract amendment, and a five-year law enforcement agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office. The Council also took up a contested appeal of a Planning Commission decision denying a 25-lot residential subdivision on Pierce Road, along with several final map approvals, a budget amendment, and a new no-parking zone near Chester Avenue and Arcadia Palms Drive.
keyTopics: Appeal of Planning Commission denial of a 25-lot residential subdivision on a 72.45-acre Pierce Road parcel, including the Environmental Impact Report certification
Five-year law enforcement services agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office
Contracts for replacing the Bellgrove Park playground
Purchase of electrical equipment to replace aging gas systems at the Warner Hutton House, Civic Center Theater, and Joan Pisani Community Center
Final map approvals for lot splits at 19200 Shubert Drive, 12468 Ted Avenue, and El Camino Senda

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — August 25, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered several infrastructure and facilities items, including roof repairs at the History Museum, EV chargers at the Maintenance Yard, and completion of the Woodland Library patio expansion. The Council also held a public hearing on a resident petition to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street, and reviewed two housing development proposals for condominium projects on First Street and near Sherwood and Acacia Avenues.
keyTopics: Public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Vesting tentative maps for 19 condominium units at 349 First Street and 33 units near Sherwood/Acacia Avenues
History Museum roof replacement contract with Diablo Roofing (not-to-exceed $147,500 plus contingency)
Maintenance Yard EV Chargers construction contract with Bockmon & Woody Electric Co. (not-to-exceed $363,220)
Draft responses to Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's BART Silicon Valley Phase II oversight

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council took up routine business including approval of prior meeting minutes, financial and payroll reports, and a professional services agreement, along with appointing a voting delegate for a League of California Cities event. The Council also considered a batch of minor updates to the Town Code and a request regarding an appeals hearing.
keyTopics: Approval of August 4, 2026 Town Council meeting minutes
Agreement for professional services and a second amendment to an existing agreement
Monthly financial and investment report for June 2026
Voting delegate and alternate appointment for the League of California Cities Annual event
Omnibus ordinance making minor updates to the Town Code, and a request to continue or hear a public hearing on appeals

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 26, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the upcoming September 1, 2026 City Council agenda, including possible additions and scheduling of time-certain items. The committee also considered a VEBA Advisory Committee appointment and a joint special meeting with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee; the September 8, 2026 draft agenda review was cancelled.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 1, 2026 City Council agenda
Assignment of time-certain scheduling for agenda items
VEBA Advisory Committee appointment
Joint special meeting with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee
Public record covering August 13-20, 2026

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — August 25, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council held a closed session to take up two confidential personnel matters: a performance evaluation of its two council-appointed employees, the City Clerk and City Manager, and labor negotiation discussions involving those same unrepresented positions. The meeting also included a public comment period for items not on the agenda.
keyTopics: Public comment period for non-agenda items
Performance evaluation of the City Clerk and City Manager
Labor negotiations regarding the unrepresented City Clerk and City Manager positions, with Vice Mayor Clark as the designated negotiator

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting that began with a closed session, followed by a separate public session focused on a presentation. The public portion covered an update on the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session (special meeting)
CleanWater Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss an upcoming Bike Fest event and a Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program. Commissioners also heard about a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI and reviewed minutes from a prior meeting.
keyTopics: Bike Fest planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program
Presentation on youth-led organization Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, allowing one councilmember to participate remotely from India while others attended in person or via Zoom. The agenda excerpt provided mainly covers logistics for public participation rather than substantive policy items.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal's remote participation from Panchkula, India
Hybrid meeting format with in-person and Zoom options for the public
Procedures for submitting written public comment before the meeting

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 11, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered introducing an ordinance amending part of the Municipal Code, and received an educational presentation on the basics of municipal bonds. The meeting also included routine business such as approving prior meeting minutes and reviewing upcoming agenda items.
keyTopics: Introduction of an ordinance amending Municipal Code Title XIII, Chapters B.6
Presentation on Municipal Bonds 101
Review of the City Council calendar of meetings
Approval of City Council meeting minutes
Preview of anticipated items for the next regular City Council meeting

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Public Art Commission — August 20, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Public Art Commission reviewed final plans for a new public art installation at 3150 El Camino Real, with a presentation from the project's art consultant, artist, and developer team. The Commission also considered funding for temporary interactive media art installations and the acceptance of donated artworks by two local artists into the city's collection.
keyTopics: Final review of public art plan for the 3150 El Camino Real private development, presented by art consultant Danielle Wohl, artist Giles Miller, and Acclaim Companies
Approval of up to $70,000 in Art in Public Places CIP funds for Code:ART 2027 temporary interactive media installations
Acceptance of donated artworks by CASP artists Adrienne Defendi and Eric Fei into the city's public art collection
Approval of June 18, 2026 Public Art Commission meeting minutes
